# Fork only: THE list of this host's system paths every fleet job sees, read-only, one per line. The only place of
# this rule: fork-fleet-launch.sh (job_fs) gives a job's unit these paths and nothing else of the host's files (its own
# copy, the hook, resolv.conf, and systemd's own /proc, /sys, /dev and memory file systems aside), and the per-OS walls
# read it through the launcher (`paths`). A path this host does not have is skipped; a symlink here (/bin -> usr/bin)
# is the same symlink in the unit; any other path is bound from its real path (links above it resolved); each is one
# mount, without what is mounted under it. A host's own extra (a tool cache) goes in launch.conf's ALLOW_PATHS, not
# here. Never a path that holds data: the launcher refuses /home, /root, /mnt, /media and /srv (also through a link),
# and the per-OS walls refuse a share.
# /etc is never here whole (issue #243): a job sees only the entries below, each one a build needs and none that holds a
# secret, so a password file, a login file, a unit, cron, /etc/default or a backup tool's folder is simply not in its
# file system. The launcher refuses /etc itself, and check-net lists the job's /etc and fails on anything else.
/usr
/bin
/sbin
/lib
/lib32
/lib64
/libx32
# Users and names: whoami, git, ssh and Node's os.userInfo() read passwd and group through nsswitch.conf; hosts has
# localhost; host.conf and gai.conf steer glibc's resolver (resolv.conf is the launcher's own, RESOLV_CONF).
/etc/passwd
/etc/group
/etc/nsswitch.conf
/etc/hosts
/etc/host.conf
/etc/gai.conf
# TLS: the CA bundle and OpenSSL's config (curl, git, Python, the runner; /usr/lib/ssl links here). Not ssl/private.
# Fedora-style hosts keep the same in pki: its certificates only, not pki/tls/private.
/etc/ssl/certs
/etc/ssl/openssl.cnf
/etc/pki/tls/certs
/etc/pki/tls/openssl.cnf
/etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted
# Programs and libraries: /usr/bin/cc, c++, ld and the like are links through alternatives; ld.so finds libraries here.
/etc/alternatives
/etc/ld.so.cache
/etc/ld.so.conf
/etc/ld.so.conf.d
# Time, locale and system facts: localtime and timezone, os-release (the runner and .NET read it), lsb-release,
# locale.alias (glibc's locale names), protocols and services (getprotobyname, getservbyname), mime.types, fonts
# (fontconfig: a browser in a test), login.defs (UID ranges some tools read).
/etc/localtime
/etc/timezone
/etc/os-release
/etc/lsb-release
/etc/locale.alias
/etc/protocols
/etc/services
/etc/mime.types
/etc/fonts
/etc/login.defs
